summary: The statement and proof are correct. The truncated height-tail factors decrease with coordinate energy relative to the untruncated Gibbs weights, giving the stated conditional high-occupation bounds even with the weighted core. Averaging these bounds and the explicit uniform coupling validly dominate Q by an independent Bernoulli sum of mean mu. The factorial tail bound, threshold split, linear exponential-moment estimate, and Cauchy-Schwarz calculation yield exactly the claimed K(a). The zero-height, zero-temperature-parameter, empty-J, equality, and zero-mean boundary cases introduce no error or gap.
